chunks: From him, from ʿAbbād ibn Sulaymān, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:

A man wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: May a man perform sajdah upon a garment by which he protects his face from the heat and the cold, and from a thing upon which he dislikes to perform sajdah? He said: Yes, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or cloth used beneath the face
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform sajdah on a garment to protect oneself from heat or cold?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting sajdah on a garment when it is used as protection from heat, cold, or something disliked for prostration. It reflects practical ease in the rulings of worship while addressing circumstances affecting salat (prayer).
